newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish roaster sees continued coffee price rises.
newsitem.headline: Finnish roaster sees continued coffee price rises.

text.p: Leading Finnish roaster Paulig Oy, which also has over 10 percent of the British coffee market, expects continued upward pressure in world coffee prices until the end of August, a Paulig official told Reuters on Friday.
"The trend seems still to be rising and this will continue until the risk of frost in Brazil ends, at the end of August," said Paulig purchasing director Jouko Pihkanen.

World coffee prices have rocketed to over $2 per lb from $1.20 at the end of 1996 and Paulig plans a 20 percent hike in wholesale prices in Finland in April, lagging behind an international 50 percent wholesale price increase, he said.
The British market situation was not yet clear.
"The pressure to up prices there is similar," he said, though the picture was blurred by the dominance of instant coffee.

Prices for consumers in Finland would rise by two to three markka from the start of April as a result of Paulig's hike, and even if world coffee prices stablised now, there would be pressure for more, Pihkanen said.
"We are already at a stage where there is pressure for more, this is only the beginning in that sense," he said.
However, at some stage higher prices would begin to dent surplus demand in some areas, he added.
